stories.title: National knife crime week of action starts in Flintshire South today
stories.summary: North Wales Police are running a knife amnesty in Broughton and Buckley today as part of Operation Sceptre, a national week of action against knife crime. A knife amnesty bin will be on Buckley High Street between 2.30pm and 4.30pm this afternoon, with PC Preece and PCSO Roberts taking in any surrendered knives. PC Gregory

stories.title: Man, 27, in custody on wounding charge after Presthaven Sands incident
stories.summary: A 27-year-old man has been charged in connection with a wounding. Jake Cooper, of Timperley Close, Oldham, is charged with wounding with intent following a domestic incident at Presthaven Sands holiday park in Prestatyn. It was reported to police in the early hours of Saturday 16 May. Cooper was arrested and subsequently remanded into custody

stories.title: Seven Flintshire stations now accept contactless tap-in rail payments
stories.summary: Rail passengers at seven Flintshire stations can now tap in and tap out with a contactless card after Transport for Wales (TfW) launched its pay as you go scheme today. stories.title: New Welsh Cabinet meets for first time with NHS waiting lists among five priorities
stories.summary: First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth will today chair the first meeting of the new Welsh Government Cabinet. Cutting NHS waiting lists, supporting families with the cost of living, creating jobs, raising standards in education and tackling child poverty are the five priorities set out by the new administration.
